claims.text: Adding approximately 5 at.% Cu and applying a post-deposition homogenization treatment will form Cu-rich conduction pathways in the HEA.
Cu-rich pathways will improve heat transfer in the HEA.
The Cu addition and homogenization treatment will preserve the alloy's structural integrity.
The baseline intermediate-layer HEA has a conventional multicomponent, single-phase or near-single-phase microstructure.
Homogenization can produce fine, controlled Cu segregation along grain boundaries or as dispersed interconnected second-phase channels.
Operating temperatures of 600–800°C under cyclic mechanical loading in inert or high-vacuum conditions are typical service conditions for plasma-facing reactor components.
The proposed structural mediator is a network of Cu-rich regions embedded in the HEA matrix, including grain-boundary pathways or continuous networks.
Copper has intrinsically high thermal conductivity.
Cu-rich phases will act as preferential channels for heat transfer through the alloy.
The bulk HEA matrix will retain high strength and resistance to plastic deformation despite the Cu-rich regions.
The bulk HEA matrix will maintain irradiation resistance after the proposed modification.
The modified HEA may achieve approximately a 20% increase in thermal conductivity relative to the Cu-free baseline.
The modified HEA will retain most of its structural strength, with only a minor or negligible reduction in yield strength.
The heat-transfer improvement and preservation of strength are expected to persist at 600–800°C under cyclic loading.
Severe irradiation or substantially different environments could prevent formation or retention of the desired Cu network or reduce toughness.
